profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Flexential cluster spans Georgia (Alpharetta, Douglasville, Norcross), Florida (Fort Lauderdale, Jacksonville, Tampa), North Carolina (Charlotte, Morrisville), and Tennessee (Brentwood, Franklin), the historic Southeastern United States footprint of Peak 10. According to Flexential own company history page, Peak 10 was founded in 2000 and built a strong regional presence across the Southeastern US. In 2017 Peak 10 purchased ViaWest, merging the two regionally dominant data center providers, and the combined company rebranded as Flexential in 2018. Flexential also acquired AppliedTrust and INetU in 2015 to expand its professional services and cloud offerings. Flexential operates 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets under CEO Ryan Mallory. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Charlotte - North in Charlotte, North Carolina, publishes 3.3 MW of IT capacity across 62,589 square feet of technical space, operated by Flexential.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 330 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 82 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Charlotte - North holds 6 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system), SSAE 18 (the attestation standard underlying SOC reports). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

North Carolina has 6 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 5 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.47 MW. Flexential Charlotte - North contributes 3.3 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
